findings.title: Installer destroys pre-existing agent instruction files without preserving differences
findings.evidence: Lines 168-171 remove any regular .cursorrules/.windsurfrules/.codexrules/CLAUDE.md/.clinerules/.roorules and replace it with a link; lines 179-181 do the same for Copilot. No backup or content preservation occurs. .babylon60rules requires preserving differences before replacing regular files.
findings.trigger: Install Shield in a project with existing custom regular instruction files.
findings.impact: Existing project instructions are irreversibly lost from the working directory.

findings.title: A contender removes an active installer lock after approximately one second
findings.evidence: acquire_lock unconditionally rm -rf removes LOCK_DIR after 200 failed mkdir attempts with sleep 0.005; no owner PID, liveness, or ownership check exists. release_lock also deletes whichever lock currently exists.
findings.trigger: Two installs/uninstalls overlap and the first takes more than the fixed wait interval.
findings.impact: Both processes can enter the critical section and race on global skills, configuration and workspace rules.

findings.title: Uninstall deletes unrelated symlinked instruction files
findings.evidence: The uninstall loop checks only -L and immediately rm -f; unlike installation it never verifies readlink target or an installation ownership manifest.
findings.trigger: Run --uninstall in a project whose CLAUDE.md or other listed instruction file links to a user-maintained source.
findings.impact: The unrelated project instruction link is removed even when Shield did not create it.

findings.title: Ledger model field reaches innerHTML without escaping
findings.evidence: HUD lines 516-525 interpolate r.model_id into tbody.innerHTML. server.rs:118-139 accepts req.model and passes it directly to evaluate_and_seal; gate.rs:91-100 stores model.to_string() in recent_receipts. Router lines 53-62 show no route authentication layer.
findings.trigger: A caller able to access the local chat endpoint submits a model string containing active HTML, then an operator opens or refreshes the ledger tab.
findings.impact: Stored script-capable markup executes in the HUD origin and can read or modify the local UI and call same-origin endpoints. Static source trace only; no browser exploit executed.

findings.title: HUD reports verified compliance from the existence of a response or receipt
findings.evidence: The response badge hardcodes ESTADO: CONFORME EU AI ACT and ledger line 522 hardcodes VERIFICADO (ART. 12-14). No verification status is evaluated. gate.rs:97 likewise assigns a constant compliance string, and server.rs:146-198 generates formatted response templates.
findings.trigger: Any chat response with choices, including the default model branch, or any receipt listed in the HUD.
findings.impact: The interface presents a compliance verification as completed without displaying evidence or a verifier decision; scope is the UI claim, not a legal assessment.

findings.title: Seqlock stress oracle accepts mixed finite snapshots and even zero successful reads
findings.evidence: Reader accepts every snapshot whose kinetic_energy and enstrophy are not NaN; all writer values at lines 406-414 are finite. It does not compare fields to epoch_id. RetryExhausted increments a counter; final assertion at 439 checks only total_torn == 0 and ignores _total_valid/_total_exhausted.
findings.trigger: The example reads fields from different publications, reads initial zero state before the writer, or exhausts every read.
findings.impact: The example can print coherence validated at 100% despite never establishing a coherent publication. This is a defect in the example validation, not evidence of an actual production torn read.

findings.title: Queue acknowledgement guidance reverses the first-call-wins contract
findings.evidence: Lines 95-105 say last call wins and demonstrate ack(); retry() as causing retry. Official Cloudflare documentation https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/configuration/batching-retries/ states the first ack/retry wins and subsequent calls are ignored (retrieved 2026-10-28).
findings.trigger: A consumer follows the example by acknowledging a message and subsequently trying to retry it after discovering a processing failure.
findings.impact: The message remains acknowledged and is not retried, risking loss of intended work. This is documentation/example guidance, not a traced production consumer.

findings.title: WAF score examples block clean traffic and spare the most suspicious requests
findings.evidence: Lines 64-68 block cf.waf.score gt 50 and SQLi/XSS scores gt 30; lines 172-173 repeat the reversed comparisons. Official https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/detections/attack-score/ documents 1 as almost certainly malicious and 99 as likely clean (retrieved 2026-10-28).
findings.trigger: Deploy the documented custom-score rules to an applicable Cloudflare zone.
findings.impact: Likely clean requests are blocked/challenged while scores 1-20 evade these score rules; other independent rules may still mitigate them.

findings.title: Advertised 90-second polling bound does not bound network reads
findings.evidence: Both urlopen calls at lines 51 and 68 omit timeout; the elapsed-time condition at 89 executes only between calls. A stalled response can block inside urlopen/read past the deadline.
findings.trigger: The remote endpoint stalls during connection, response headers or body while run_fsm is polling.
findings.impact: The PoC can hang indefinitely instead of enforcing its declared 90-second bound.

hypotheses.note: Catalog includes clinical indications and dated references; textual coverage is complete, but a systematic clinical fact-check and downstream consumption audit were outside this shard. No medical correctness guarantee is inferred.
